Please review the following manuscript. I've poured days of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-6i4wu2ru/call-54979a3576d24e6c9b3eb8915e2a0f18/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for m in ['fitz','pymupdf','pypdf','pdfplumber','PIL']:
    print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES', len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    t=p.extract_text()
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
    print(f'PAGE {i+1}: {len(t)} chars; size {p.mediabox}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.extract_text() for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    links=[]
    for a in p.get('/Annots',[]):
        obj=a.get_object()
        act=obj.get('/A',{})
        uri=act.get('/URI')
        if uri:
            links.append(uri)
    if links:
        print(i+1, '\\n'.join(links))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important efficiency problem in vision-language models. Reusing CLIP attention for adaptive token selection and key similarity for merging offers a simple mechanism that requires no additional learned token selector.

PruMerge+ demonstrates a useful compression–accuracy tradeoff. With a reported 25% of visual tokens, the 7B model achieves 76.8 versus 78.5 on VQAv2 and 64.9 versus 64.3 on MMBench (Table 1). Evaluation spans six image benchmarks and two language-model sizes.

The training-free Video-LLaVA experiments provide encouraging transfer evidence across three benchmarks. PruMerge improves ActivityNet-QA accuracy from 45.3 to 48.3 while retaining broadly similar performance on the other video benchmarks (Table 3).

The ablations provide evidence for individual design choices. PruMerge outperforms spatial sampling at comparable average token budgets, and adding token supplementation improves MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 (Tables 4–5). Table 6 also distinguishes training-free performance from improvements obtained through fine-tuning.

The figures communicate the overall pipeline effectively, and the principal backbone models, training data, benchmarks, and methodological antecedents are identified and cited. The appendix appropriately acknowledges lossy compression, limited validation scope, and potential misuse.
weaknesses: The central practical efficiency claims lack measured validation. Table 2 explicitly reports roofline estimates for LLM prefill, rather than actual latency or memory measurements. It does not establish end-to-end gains after visual encoding, selection/merging overhead, variable-length batching, and decoding. Measurements for both PruMerge and the more accurate PruMerge+ are needed to establish the deployment benefit.

The aggressive compression results do not support repeated claims of preserving performance without compromise. Even after fine-tuning, 7B PruMerge drops from 78.5 to 72.0 on VQAv2, 85.9 to 76.3 on POPE, and 1510.7 to 1350.3 on MME (Table 1). These tradeoffs may be valuable, but describing them as marginal understates their magnitude. Section 4.1 also incorrectly claims an improvement on POPE.

The comparative evidence does not sufficiently establish the contribution over existing token-reduction ideas. Table 4 compares against first-N and uniform spatial sampling, but lacks fixed-budget attention top-k selection and an adapted key-similarity merging baseline such as the cited ToMe. Consequently, the specific benefit of adaptive IQR selection remains unclear. Comparisons at matched token budgets, including the PruMerge+ operating point, would substantially strengthen the scientific case.

Important algorithmic details impede reproduction. Algorithm 1 replaces each selected center with an unnormalized weighted sum of other tokens, whereas the introduction describes weighted averaging and supplementation. The manuscript does not specify the neighbor count k or how attention and keys are aggregated across heads. Section 3.3 refers to final-layer keys, while Algorithm 1 specifies the penultimate layer. LoRA settings beyond the dataset and one training epoch are also missing.

The PruMerge+ token budget is inconsistent with its specification. Algorithm 1 adds m uniformly sampled tokens to m selected tokens, implying approximately twice the original retained fraction; this does not explain the reported increase from 5.5% to 25% in Table 1. The subsequent loop and output still reference only m tokens. Resolving the actual sampling rule and output size is essential because these determine the principal accuracy–compression tradeoff.
